nominees.name: Ned Lamont
nominees.role: Democratic incumbent governor seeking a third term

positions.stance: Keeps middle-class income tax cuts, expanded EITC rates, senior exemptions and the motor-vehicle tax cap; eliminates sales tax on school supplies; raises Sales Tax-Free Week ceiling to $300; converts THC tax to a 10.75% excise tax (Governor's press release).

About $193 million in supplemental K-12 grants; more than $100 million one-time to lower local property taxes; about $300 million for the Early Childhood Education Endowment; universal free school breakfast.
Over $1 billion in extra pension payments in each of FY2026 and FY2027; Federal Cuts Response Fund up $50 million; $813.7 million of volatile revenue spent under a governor's declaration.

policyShifts.shift: Continued large pension paydowns and a federal-cuts response fund.
More one-time local aid to hold down property taxes.

impediments.title: Federal cuts
impediments.detail: A larger Federal Cuts Response Fund signals expected federal reductions; Medicaid shortfalls cited ($80 million).

impediments.title: Volatility cap
impediments.detail: Spending of surplus depends on a governor's declaration under the volatility cap.

insights: Third-term incumbent: expect continuity in the budget framework; personnel change is incremental. These figures are from the governor's own release.
Sources for Lamont's third-term agenda beyond the FY2027 budget were not opened.

analysis.assumption: Scenario: assumes Ned Lamont wins the Nov. 3, 2026 general election. AP has called this race (AP lookup, Nov. 4, 2026 04:16 UTC); this tool does not make calls. Not a call or forecast.
analysis.summary: Incumbent continuity: fiscal-guardrail budgeting, municipal aid and pension payments.
